prompt: Why does a production prompt live in one file with a history, rather than one file per version?

choices.text: One file is cheaper to send to the model
choices.why: The model receives the same text either way.

choices.text: Prompt files cannot be compared side by side
choices.why: They can; nothing says which was live.

choices.text: A program reads one path, and git records the order
choices.why: Right: which one is live, and since when.

choices.text: Git refuses to store more than one prompt file
choices.why: It stores any number.

prompt: Why are the commit hashes in this lesson the same as the ones `history.sh` makes for you?
hint: What goes into a commit hash?

choices.text: The dates and author are in the script
choices.why: Right: same content, same dates, same hashes.

choices.text: Git hashes only the commit message
choices.why: It hashes the tree, the author, the dates and the parent too.

choices.text: Ollama assigns the hashes from the model id
choices.why: Ollama has nothing to do with git.

choices.text: The hashes are random and happen to match
choices.why: Nothing about them is random.

prompt: What does `git diff 5b2d8d0 a0f1d2a -- prompts/triage.txt` tell you that the two commit messages do not?

choices.text: Whether the change improved the score
choices.why: Git knows nothing about scores.

choices.text: Who reviewed the change before it went in
choices.why: A diff shows lines, not reviewers.

choices.text: How many tokens the new prompt costs per call
choices.why: That needs a run.

choices.text: Which lines were added and removed
choices.why: Right: what was done, not what was meant.

prompt: To print the file as it was at commit `c8f1927`, you run `git ___ c8f1927:prompts/triage.txt`.
`pl run` printed the id `c1916fcd` for today's file and for the copy taken from commit `c8f1927`. Why are they equal?

choices.text: The id counts the commits that touched the file
choices.why: It is not a counter.

choices.text: The id hashes the bytes, and they are equal
choices.why: Right: the revert restored the same bytes.

choices.text: `pl` reuses the id of the newest commit
choices.why: `pl` knows nothing about commits.

choices.text: Both runs used the same test set
choices.why: The id comes from the prompt alone.

prompt: Running `prompts/triage.txt` with `--set temperature=0.8` kept the id `c1916fcd`. How many of the 40 dev messages passed every check?
Why should `temperature` be written above the `---` in the prompt file rather than passed with `--set`?

choices.text: `--set` only works for the model's name
choices.why: It works for any setting.

choices.text: A header makes the prompt cheaper to run
choices.why: Cost is not the reason.

choices.text: Written in the file, it changes the id
choices.why: Right: two different prompts get two ids.

choices.text: Ollama ignores settings passed on the command line
choices.why: It receives them; nothing records them.

prompt: Which of these belong to a version of a prompt, in the lesson's sense? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four, and a fifth no file holds.

choices.text: The text
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The parameters in its header
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The model and its exact build
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The name of the person who ran it
choices.why: The author is in git; it is not what makes a result rebuildable.

prompt: A provider moves a short model alias to a newer model. Your prompt file names the alias and has not changed. What has happened to your prompt?

choices.text: It is a different prompt under the same id
choices.why: Right: name the dated model in the header.

choices.text: Its test set has become invalid
choices.why: The test set still measures; what it measures moved.

choices.text: Git will show the change as a diff
choices.why: Nothing in the repository changed.

choices.text: Nothing, since the file and its id are the same
choices.why: The id cannot see the model behind an alias.

prompt: What does `log.py` print for each commit of `prompts/triage.txt`?

choices.text: The diff against the commit before it
choices.why: That is `git diff`.

choices.text: The commit's author and the time it took to run
choices.why: It prints the date and the subject, not the time taken.

choices.text: Only the commits whose score went up
choices.why: It prints every commit.

choices.text: How many passed every check, and the tokens used
choices.why: Right.

prompt: `5b2d8d0` used 11726 tokens over the forty dev calls and `ab97290` used 11152. How many extra tokens per call did the new instruction cost? One decimal place.
`a0f1d2a` added 1682 tokens on dev and the score fell from 26 to 24. What did `log.py cases/attacks.jsonl` show about it?
hint: The set it was written for.

choices.text: It could not be run on the attacks
choices.why: It ran like every other commit.

choices.text: It took the attacks from 2 to 3
choices.why: Right: dev does not test what it was for.

choices.text: It broke every attack it had passed
choices.why: It gained one.

choices.text: It made no difference on the attacks either
choices.why: It was the only commit after the examples to move them.

prompt: `86913c0` rewrote the examples as plain lines, and the score went from 24 to 27 with fewer tokens. Why did the replies stay valid JSON?
hint: What else in the prompt asks for JSON?

choices.text: The plain lines were valid JSON
choices.why: `billing, normal: ...` is not JSON.

choices.text: `pl check --lenient` was used for this run
choices.why: `log.py` uses the strict `judge()`.

choices.text: The instruction and the field list asked for it
choices.why: Right: on this model the examples carried the labels.

choices.text: Ollama converts every reply to JSON
choices.why: Ollama returns what the model wrote.

prompt: A change leaves every test set's score where it was and adds 40 tokens per call. What does the lesson say to do?

choices.text: Add the case it fixes, or say it fixes nothing
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Ship it, since the scores did not fall
choices.why: A change no set can see is taken on trust.

choices.text: Run it at a higher temperature to see an effect
choices.why: That measures something else.

choices.text: Revert it, since it costs tokens and moves nothing
choices.why: It may fix something no set tests.

prompt: In the gate the lesson describes, which line of `pl compare` decides whether a change is stopped?

choices.text: `passes`
choices.why: Totals hide moves in both directions.

choices.text: The sign test's p
choices.why: The p says how unusual the split is, not what broke.

choices.text: The prompt id
choices.why: The id identifies the file, not the result.

choices.text: `broken`
choices.why: Right: any broken message stops it, or needs a reason.

prompt: Comparing the live `86913c0` with the revert on dev, how many messages did `pl compare` list as broken?
The run at temperature 0.8 broke one message and fixed another. Why would a gate that runs only when the prompt file changes miss it?

choices.text: The prompt id changed and confused the gate
choices.why: The id stayed the same.

choices.text: The change was never in the file
choices.why: Right: put every parameter in the file.

choices.text: One message is too few for the gate to notice
choices.why: The gate fails on any broken message.

choices.text: Temperature changes are invisible to `pl compare`
choices.why: `pl compare` showed it.

prompt: Which of these belong to the gate the section describes? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: It runs on every change to a prompt file
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: It runs every test set the prompt has
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: It fails on any broken message and names them
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: It passes any change that raises the total
choices.why: A total can rise while messages break.

prompt: Put these steps for a change to `prompts/triage.txt` in the order the lesson implies.
hint: The gate comes before the merge.
items: Edit the file and commit it on a branch
Run the new and the live file on every test set
Compare them and read the broken messages
Merge, or explain in the commit why not

prompt: Match each commit to what `log.py` showed about it.
A teammate reports 24 of 40 for 'the triage prompt' in a chat message, with no id. What is missing before anybody can rebuild that result?

choices.text: Only the name of the test set
choices.why: That is one part of four.

choices.text: Nothing: 24 of 40 is the whole result
choices.why: A score belongs to a version.

choices.text: Its id, model, settings and test set
choices.why: Right: and the machine it ran on.

choices.text: Only the date of the run
choices.why: A date does not say which file.
